events.extended_summary: The Trump administration announced plans to impose new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China, the European Union and India, accusing them of flooding markets with cheap goods through unfair subsidies and suppressed wages. China faces the highest rate at 20 percent, matching the truce rate from last year's Trump-Xi deal expiring in mid-January. The move follows a Supreme Court ruling declaring previous "Liberation Day" tariffs illegal, prompting the administration to rebuild leverage under a new legal basis. Tariffs take effect in January or February after consultation, with announced rates serving as upper ceilings open to negotiation. Beijing responded with muted criticism, calling overcapacity a "false issue" and urging implementation of the existing agreement. The UK remains unaffected but stays subject to 10 percent tariffs under forced labour provisions. Twenty-five states have sued to challenge those forced labour tariffs.
events.micro_summary: The Trump administration announced new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China at 20 percent to rebuild trade leverage.
events.summary: The US announced new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China at 20 percent, the EU and India, citing unfair subsidies and excess capacity, with rates set to take effect in January or February after consultation.

events.extended_summary: Spain holds a snap election on Sunday with almost 39 million eligible voters casting ballots. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, whose coalition collapsed after failing to pass housing crisis measures, trails the center-right People's Party led by Alberto Núñez Feijóo in polls. Sánchez has expressed confidence in defying the polls and accused Feijóo of planning a coalition with the far-right Vox party, while Feijóo promised a new era of "truth, decency and good governance" and accused Sánchez of evading questions on corruption, rail disasters, immigration and national debt. If the right wins, it would likely form a governing coalition between the PP and Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, marking the first such right-wing government since the death of Francisco Franco. Under Spanish electoral law, no polls have been published since Monday. The election comes amid strikes, housing affordability crises and economic concerns, with commentators expecting high turnout and close finish.
events.micro_summary: Spain votes Sunday in snap election with Socialist PM Sánchez trailing conservative PP in polls ahead of possible right-wing coalition.
events.summary: Spain votes Sunday in a snap election with almost 39 million eligible voters, as Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez trails the conservative People's Party in polls, with a potential PP-Vox coalition looming if the right wins.

events.extended_summary: Puma Shen of the Democratic Progressive Party is in a tight race against incumbent Chiang Wan-an of the Kuomintang to become Taipei's next mayor in Saturday's election. Shen, who founded a prominent civil defence organisation and was sanctioned by China two years ago as a 'diehard' separatist, takes a more combative approach to Beijing than his opponent. The contest could shape Taiwan's 2028 presidential run, where cross-strait issues will dominate. Taipei has not had a DPP mayor since 1998. China favours the KMT, whose chairman met President Xi Jinping earlier this year, while Beijing refers to President Lai Ching-te as a 'destroyer' of peace. A Shen victory, combined with a DPP win in neighbouring New Taipei City, could embolden the party ahead of 2028. In 2022 local elections the KMT won 15 seats to the DPP's six, though the DPP won more seats and the presidency in 2024.
events.micro_summary: Puma Shen races incumbent Chiang Wan-an for Taipei mayor in a tight contest shaping Taiwan's 2028 presidential run.
events.summary: Puma Shen of the DPP faces incumbent Chiang Wan-an of the KMT in a tight Taipei mayoral race that could shape the 2028 presidential election, with Shen sanctioned by Beijing as a 'diehard' separatist.

events.extended_summary: During a visit to Berlin, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, La France insoumise's candidate in the French presidential election, called for a thorough overhaul of the French-German relationship. The 75-year-old politician, polling in second place and favourite to reach a run-off against Marine Le Pen, criticised Germany's economic dominance in the European Union and its record military spending. He expressed deep concern about German rearmament, noting Germany's military budget is set to reach €139.4 billion in 2027, more than twice the €63.3 billion planned for French defence. Mélenchon questioned Chancellor Friedrich Merz's commitment to making the German military the strongest conventional army in Europe, asking "to make war against whom?" and warning that Germany's growing military strength makes it a target. He met with Ines Schwerdtner, national leader of Die Linke, stating they were united against an economy of rearmament. Mélenchon denied charges of being Germanophobic, calling himself a disciple of Karl Marx.
events.micro_summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon called for an overhaul of French-German ties during a Berlin visit, criticizing Germany's €139.4 billion military budget.
events.summary: During a Berlin visit, French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon called for an overhaul of ties with Germany, criticizing its economic dominance and €139.4 billion 2027 military budget, and questioning the purpose of German rearmament.

events.extended_summary: A Russian triple-tap strike hit the center of Kryvyi Rih, President Volodymyr Zelensky's hometown, on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic and wounding 60 others. Ballistic missiles struck a restaurant parking lot, followed by jet-powered drones targeting rescue workers responding to the initial blast, and a third drone strike shortly after. The attack caused four fires and damaged approximately 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, businesses and vehicles. Among the wounded were six children, with 28 people remaining hospitalized, including a three-year-old girl, and five in intensive care. The strike occurred on Children's Day in Ukraine, near a popular restaurant in the city center where no military facilities are located. The boy, identified as Tikhon, was visiting the city with his family, and two of his brothers were among those in intensive care.
events.micro_summary: Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 60, including a seven-year-old boy.
events.summary: A Russian triple-tap strike on Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's hometown, killed a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic Friday night, wounding 60 others, including six children, and damaging 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools.

events.extended_summary: Research using Sentinel-1 satellite radar imagery reveals that some of Africa's largest coastal cities are sinking faster than previously estimated. Scientists mapped land movement beneath 20 African coastal cities, finding Lagos, Nigeria and Alexandria, Egypt sinking at average rates of 5mm and 6mm per year respectively. Human activities such as groundwater extraction drive this subsidence, which compounds sea level rise from climate change. The study estimates that by 2050, seven million people, one billion buildings and $180bn in assets across these cities could face flood risk, with five million people and $150bn in assets exposed in Lagos and Alexandria alone. Four million people in Lagos may be exposed to extreme sea levels by the end of the century. Using over 4,000 satellite images, researchers detected land movements as small as 1mm per year, overcoming previous monitoring limitations.
events.micro_summary: Lagos and Alexandria sink 5mm and 6mm yearly, putting seven million people at flood risk by 2050.
events.summary: Satellite data shows Lagos and Alexandria are sinking 5mm and 6mm per year, and with rising seas could expose seven million people, one billion buildings and $180bn in assets to flooding by 2050.

events.extended_summary: NATO fighter jets conducted simulated ground strikes and air superiority missions during the Protective Fence 26 military exercise in northern Finland near the Russian border. For the first time, the French Air and Space Force deployed three Rafale multirole fighter jets to the Arctic-region exercise, joining Finnish F/A-18 Hornets, Dutch F-35A Lightning IIs, and Swedish JAS 39 Gripens. The training took place at the Jännevirta highway strip, approximately 104 miles from the Russian border, and included air-to-ground attacks, air superiority operations, simulated airspace-entry Entry Force missions, and Defensive Counter Air scenarios. The exercise allowed participating NATO air forces to practice combined air operations involving four different fighter aircraft types in demanding Arctic conditions.
events.micro_summary: Three French Rafale jets participated in NATO's Protective Fence 26 exercise in northern Finland near Russia.
events.summary: NATO fighter jets conducted simulated strikes and air superiority missions during the Protective Fence 26 exercise in northern Finland near the Russian border, with three French Rafale jets participating for the first time alongside Finnish, Dutch, and Swedish aircraft.

events.extended_summary: Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice to lead Nottingham Forest to a 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground, deepening the crisis for Xabi Alonso's side. Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes, and Gibbs-White converted a penalty early in the second half after Wesley Fofana conceded it. Gibbs-White added a second goal later to reflect Forest's superiority. Emmanuel Emegha came off the bench to score twice for Chelsea, including an 89th-minute goal that made for a nervy finish, but Forest held on for their first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997. The victory lifts Forest clear of the bottom six, while Chelsea missed the chance to climb back into the top five and have now lost four of their last five Premier League games under Alonso.
events.micro_summary: Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at the City Ground.
events.summary: Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest defeated Chelsea 3-2 at the City Ground, with Igor Jesus opening the scoring in five minutes and Emmanuel Emegha scoring twice for the visitors in a nervy finale.

events.extended_summary: No. 3 Texas travels to College Station Friday to face rival Texas A&M in the Lone Star Showdown with an SEC championship game berth and a first-round College Football Playoff bye on the line. The Longhorns have won five consecutive games and can clinch a spot in the SEC Championship with a victory. Texas A&M has struggled this season, going from last year's College Football Playoff to missing a bowl game, and coach Mike Elko has yet to beat Texas in three attempts. Texas won the first two meetings since joining the SEC in 2024, including a 27-17 victory in Austin last year. During the game, Texas kicker Gianni Spetic connected on a 54-yard field goal after freshman Kohen Brown recovered a muffed punt, while quarterback Arch Manning completed passes to Emaree Winston, Emmett Mosley V, and Raleek Brown.
events.micro_summary: No. 3 Texas plays Texas A&M Friday with SEC championship and playoff berth on the line.
events.summary: No. 3 Texas faces Texas A&M in College Station Friday with an SEC championship berth and College Football Playoff first-round bye at stake. Texas has won five straight and beat the Aggies 27-17 last year.

events.extended_summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Black Friday in Pittsburgh, improving their record to 7-4 while dropping Denver to 8-3. The Steelers defense dominated, scoring twice: T.J. Watt recovered a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone for a 7-0 lead in the first quarter, and Jalen Ramsey returned an interception for a touchdown in the second quarter to make it 24-5. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix struggled, completing 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards with two interceptions, three sacks, and a 44.7 passer rating. Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph, starting for the first time since Aaron Rodgers was benched and released, completed 9 of 15 passes for 142 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. The game was played in cold, wet conditions with temperatures around 37 degrees, sleet, and wind.
events.micro_summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Black Friday.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Black Friday, improving to 7-4 behind defensive touchdowns by T.J. Watt and Jalen Ramsey.

events.extended_summary: Australia has omitted veteran spinner Nathan Lyon from its 13-man Test squad for the four-match home series against New Zealand beginning December 9. The 39-year-old, who has taken 577 Test wickets in 145 matches and served as first-choice spinner since 2013, was left out alongside Cooper Connolly, Beau Webster and Marnus Labuschagne. Uncapped pair Corey Rocchiccioli and Jack Clayton have earned call-ups, with Rocchiccioli usurping Lyon as the frontline spinner. Steve Smith returns to the side after injury, while Cameron Green is recovering from concussion. Selectors will add a 14th player following the sixth Sheffield Shield round. Selection chair George Bailey stated Lyon had not quite had the desired impact recently, though acknowledging his extraordinary record. Lyon remains determined to fight back into the side for next year's tours of India and England.
events.micro_summary: Nathan Lyon omitted from Australia's 13-man Test squad for four-Test series against New Zealand.

sources.publisher: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

events.summary: Australia named a 13-man Test squad for the four-match series against New Zealand beginning December 9, omitting veteran spinner Nathan Lyon (577 wickets) in favor of uncapped Corey Rocchiccioli and Jack Clayton.

events.extended_summary: A 14-year-old Iranian girl was beaten to death by her husband days after giving birth, campaigners have revealed. Sogand Moshtareki, from the country's Kerman province, was killed on November 6 after she had asked her 20-year-old husband if she could visit her family. The teenager, who had given birth ten days earlier, had been forced into marriage at the age of 13. Sogand's husband confessed to her murder and said the motive was 'family disputes', according to the National Council of Resistance of Iran (NCRI)'s Women Committee. The schoolgirl had recently survived a traffic accident and was still recovering when she gave birth. The Iran Human Rights (IHR) organisation said they had learned from Sogand's father that her husband had restricted her contact with family and would lock her inside the house when he went out. events.micro_summary: Teen bride, 14, beaten to death by Iranian husband, 20, days after giving birth ‘because she asked to visit her.

events.extended_summary: Alleged Russia-directed sabotage across Europe is intensifying, with the use of explosives and arson roughly doubling over the past year and presenting a risk of mass casualties as Moscow targets rail lines, airports and energy networks. Germany and Poland account for more than half of reported incidents between October 2025 and September 2026, including 29 Moscow-linked incidents in Poland. In November 2025, an explosive charge damaged a rail line linking Warsaw to the Ukraine border; though there were no casualties, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the explosion was likely planned to destroy a train. Meanwhile, new data suggests 720,000 Russian soldiers have been killed since the start of the Ukraine war. While US envoy Jared Kushner praised Vladimir Putin's restraint regarding nuclear weapons, unconventional war poses an immediate threat to Europe.
events.micro_summary: Russian-linked sabotage in Europe doubles with 29 Poland incidents and 720,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war.
events.summary: Alleged Russia-directed sabotage targeting European infrastructure has roughly doubled, with 29 Moscow-linked incidents in Poland between October 2025 and September 2026, including a rail line bombing, while new data suggests 720,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war.

events.extended_summary: A court in Mombasa, Kenya, convicted self-styled pastor Paul Mackenzie and 29 accomplices, including his wife Rhoda Mumbua Maweu, of manslaughter for the deaths of 123 adult followers. The court found Mackenzie systematically persuaded followers to fast to death in Shakahola forest between January 2021 and September 2023 as part of a suicide pact to meet Jesus, with children ordered to die first, then women, then men. Mackenzie, who pleaded not guilty and plans to appeal, was arrested in 2023 after authorities discovered more than 400 bodies in shallow graves. This conviction follows his sentencing earlier this month to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, 190 of them children. Sixty other defendants were acquitted, prompting the prosecution to announce an appeal. Mackenzie also faces separate convictions for child cruelty, assault, radicalization, and terrorism-related offenses.
events.micro_summary: Paul Mackenzie convicted of manslaughter of 123 followers in Kenya cult deaths.
events.summary: A Kenyan court convicted cult leader Paul Mackenzie and 29 others of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 followers who starved in Shakahola forest, adding to his 200-year sentence for murdering 191 people.

events.extended_summary: A massive storm hammered the US during Thanksgiving week, disrupting travel for more than 80 million Americans. On Thursday, 460 flights were cancelled and 2,508 were delayed, while nearly 980,000 households lost power, particularly in Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey. Damaging winds reached 70mph, causing coastal flooding and prompting state of emergencies in New Jersey and New York. The Macy's Thanksgiving parade was postponed to Saturday. In Maryland, almost two million customers were asked to limit water use due to power disruptions. Washington DC experienced its wettest Thanksgiving on record, with tidal flooding soaking runways at Reagan National Airport. President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds for the east coast, while Pacific storms threatened the West Coast.
events.micro_summary: A powerful Thanksgiving storm cancelled 460 flights and left nearly one million US households without power.
events.summary: A powerful Thanksgiving storm battered the US with heavy rain and winds up to 70mph, cancelling 460 flights, delaying 2,508, and leaving nearly one million households without power across Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the film has set records across North America, Europe, Southeast Asia and parts of Africa, including markets where Indian films have traditionally recorded limited business.The milestone comes as the film's worldwide gross collection reached Rs 1,777 crore in 22 days. Now in its fourth week, the mythological epic is also reportedly preparing for releases in China, Japan, South Korea and Russia in the first quarter of 2027, subject to scheduling and approvals.According to the makers, the record-setting markets include the United States and Canada, the United Kingdom, Thailand, Indonesia, Nepal, the Netherlands, Vietnam, Cambodia, South Africa and Kazakhstan. events.extended_summary: A controversy has erupted over Netflix's planned global release of Pakistani web series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo', with the Indian government asking the streaming platform to ensure that Pakistani-origin content remains unavailable to viewers in the country. The show, featuring actors Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Hamza Ali Abbasi, is scheduled to premiere on December 4. The row has intensified after a 2017 photograph of Abbasi posing for a selfie with Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed resurfaced online, bringing renewed scrutiny to the actor's past association with the Pakistan-based terrorist leader. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has asked Netflix to honour its earlier commitment not to stream Pakistani-origin films or series in India. The direction follows complaints over the upcoming show and demands from Indian film industry organisations to block its release in the country.
